title: Buttermilk Biscuits (Holly Nilsson)
attribution: Holly Nilsson, Spend With Pennies, Homemade Buttermilk Biscuits

items: 1 cup buttermilk, adjusted by about 2 tablespoons if needed

instructions: Set the oven to 450 F. Stir the flour, baking powder, sugar, baking soda, and salt together.
Cut the cold butter into the dry mixture with a pastry cutter or forks, leaving pea-size pieces.
Stir in buttermilk gradually until the dough holds together without overmixing; use a little more or less only if necessary.
On a lightly floured surface, knead briefly, pat into a square, and fold the dough over itself 5-6 times.
Pat to 1-inch thickness. Cut straight down with a sharp biscuit cutter without twisting; gather and cut the scraps.
Bake on an ungreased baking sheet for 10-12 minutes, until golden.
notes: The publisher's summary lists 20 minutes cook time, but its actual baking instruction says 10-12 minutes; the latter is preserved here. Keep the butter cold and handle the dough gently.

title: Sausage Gravy (Holly Nilsson)
attribution: Holly Nilsson, Spend With Pennies, Sausage Gravy

items: 1 tablespoon salted butter or bacon fat
2 1/3 cups whole milk, adjusted as needed for consistency
Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions: Brown the sausage over medium-high heat in a large skillet, breaking it into small pieces. Leave its rendered fat in the pan.
Melt the butter or bacon fat into the sausage. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the milk gradually while stirring to keep the gravy smooth.
Bring to a bubbling boil, then reduce to medium-low and simmer until thick. Adjust with a little milk if necessary.
Season to taste and serve hot with biscuits or potatoes.
notes: Food-safety addition: ground pork should reach 160 F. This is a full 1-pound-sausage recipe, not the half-batch adaptation on Red Door Skillet.

title: White Chocolate Raspberry Bundt Cake (Erica Walker)
attribution: Erica Walker, Favorite Family Recipes, White Chocolate Raspberry Bundt Cake

ingredient_groups.title: Cake
items: 1 package (3.4 ounces) instant white chocolate pudding mix, dry
1 cup white chocolate chips, chopped smaller

ingredient_groups.title: Cream cheese frosting
items: 3-4 cups powdered sugar, adjusted to frosting consistency

instructions: Preheat to 350 F and thoroughly grease a standard Bundt pan.
Combine the dry cake and pudding mixes with sour cream, eggs, water, and oil. Stir the chopped chips into the batter.
Put half the batter in the pan. Add 1/4 cup preserves in small dollops and swirl through the batter. Add the remaining batter and repeat with the other 1/4 cup preserves.
Bake for 45-50 minutes, checking that the center is cooked. Let the cake rest in its pan for 10 minutes, then turn it out.
Cool, cover, and refrigerate overnight before frosting.
Beat the softened cream cheese and butter together. Add vanilla and powdered sugar gradually until the frosting is thick and spreadable, using the listed 3-4 cups as the quantity range.
Spread or pipe the frosting onto the chilled cake.
notes: This is a separate whole-egg recipe, not the existing egg-white/buttermilk family card. Do not combine their ratios.
The publisher says a 3.9-ounce pudding package may be used by measuring 1/2 cup loosely packed dry mix when a 3.4-ounce package is unavailable.
Keep the Bundt pan no more than 2/3-3/4 full. Elevation can affect baking; this import preserves the base formula rather than adding unverified altitude changes.

The source frosting method starts sugar additions at 2 cups; its ingredient list specifies 3-4 cups. Add gradually within the listed range until suitable for piping. Food-safety addition: refrigerate the cream-cheese-frosted cake.

title: Crock Pot Stuffing (Holly Nilsson)
attribution: Holly Nilsson, Spend With Pennies, Crock Pot Stuffing

items: 1 tablespoon fresh thyme, sage, or rosemary, optional and adjusted to taste
3 cups chicken broth, plus up to 1 additional cup if needed

instructions: If needed, dry the bread cubes uncovered for 24 hours or in a single layer at 300 F for about 25 minutes, stirring halfway. Measure the cubes after drying.
Melt butter over medium heat. Add poultry seasoning, pepper, salt, celery, and onions; cook until softened without browning, then cool completely.
Toss the dry bread with the cooled vegetable mixture, parsley, and optional herbs.
Add broth gradually until moist but not soggy; the entire listed amount may not be needed. Stir in the eggs.
Grease a 5-6-quart slow cooker and add the stuffing. Cook on high for 30 minutes, then on low for 3-4 hours until cooked through.
Food-safety addition: check the center with a thermometer and do not serve until it reaches 165 F.
notes: Home-dried cubes may need nearer 2 cups broth; purchased dry cubes may need nearer 3 cups. Adjust to moistness rather than adding all 4 cups automatically.
For advance preparation, cover and refrigerate overnight before cooking. This is a slow-cooker formula, not Mom's original oven method or its suggested doubled egg quantity.

title: Yeast-Raised Doughnuts (Susan Reid)
attribution: Susan Reid, King Arthur Baking, Yeast-Raised Doughnuts
yield: About 16 doughnuts, depending on cutter size

items: 2 teaspoons instant yeast or active dry yeast
6 cups peanut oil or vegetable shortening for frying
Sugar, glaze, frosting, or filling as desired, optional

instructions: Stir flour, sugar, salt, yeast, and nutmeg together. Separately mix egg, milk, melted butter, and vanilla, then combine with the dry ingredients to form a soft dough. Cover and rest 5 minutes.
Knead 6-8 minutes until smooth. Put in a greased bowl, turn to coat, cover, and let rise 1 1/2-2 hours until doubled.
Deflate and roll on a lightly floured surface to 1/4-inch thickness. Cut with a 2 1/2-3-inch round cutter, cover loosely, and proof 30-60 minutes until doubled.
Heat the frying fat to 350 F in a heavy pan. Fry 2-3 doughnuts at a time, turning when golden; the source expects no more than about 1 minute per side for this formula.
Lift out and drain on absorbent paper. Verify a sample has no raw center, then add an optional coating or filling.
notes: Optional baked version from the same publisher: after shaping, proof 45-60 minutes, then bake at 350 F for about 14 minutes. Cut into a sample and continue baking if its center is raw.
These quantities and 1/4-inch shaping are for this separate recipe, not the incomplete Berliner formula. Do not transfer this timing automatically to the richer original dough.

title: Easy Bread Machine Bread (PJ Hamel)
attribution: PJ Hamel, King Arthur Baking, Easy Bread Machine Bread
yield: 1 loaf; choose ONE ingredient group for the machine's capacity

ingredient_groups.title: Large 1 1/2-2-pound machine ONLY
items: 1 1/2 teaspoons active dry yeast or instant yeast

ingredient_groups.title: Small 1-pound machine ONLY; use INSTEAD of the large group
items: 1 teaspoon active dry yeast or instant yeast

instructions: Check the machine's capacity and select just one of the two ingredient groups. Weigh flour, or spoon it into a cup and level without packing.
Load that group's ingredients in the order specified by your machine manufacturer.
Select the standard basic-white bread cycle and start. Let the machine complete its own kneading, rising, and baking cycle.
Use oven mitts to remove the hot pan. After about 5 minutes, release the loaf onto a cooling rack.
Wrap after cooling; keep at room temperature for up to 4 days or freeze for up to 3 months.
notes: The two ingredient groups are alternatives, not one combined batch. Cycle duration depends on the machine; the published recipe does not establish a rapid-cycle equivalent.

title: 100% Whole Wheat Bread Machine Bread (PJ Hamel)
attribution: PJ Hamel, King Arthur Baking, 100% Whole Wheat Bread for the Bread Machine
yield: 1 loaf; the same dough fits an 8 1/2 by 4 1/2-inch oven loaf pan

items: 2 tablespoons (25 grams) olive oil or vegetable oil
1/4 cup honey (85 grams) or maple syrup (78 grams)
3 1/2 cups (397 grams) golden whole wheat flour
1/4 cup (35 grams) sunflower, sesame, or flax seeds, optional
1 tablespoon vital wheat gluten, optional for higher rise

instructions: Weigh flour or spoon it lightly into a cup and level. Check your bread machine's flour/loaf capacity before loading this batch.
Place ingredients in the bread pan in the listed order. Select basic white or, if provided, the whole-wheat program and start.
After the machine's full cycle finishes, remove the hot pan with oven mitts and turn the loaf onto a rack. Let cool before wrapping or slicing.
notes: The publisher developed this formula for a Zojirushi machine but does not give a universal loaf-weight setting or cycle duration. Do not guess a rapid mode or use a machine too small for this flour quantity.

Complete oven alternative with the same ingredients: mix and knead 8-10 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky; cover and rise 1-1 1/2 hours until doubled. Deflate, shape in a greased 8 1/2 by 4 1/2-inch pan, and rise another 1-1 1/2 hours until doubled. Bake at 375 F about 35 minutes, until the center is 190 F, then remove from the pan and cool.
This differs materially from the existing two-loaf whole-grain wheat bread with agave and molasses; neither recipe is replaced.

title: Bread Machine Multigrain Bread (Bread Dad)
attribution: Bread Dad, Bread Machine Multigrain Bread
yield: 1 loaf, about 12 slices; choose ONE loaf-size group

ingredient_groups.title: 1.5-pound loaf
items: 3/4 cup (120 grams) dry finely chopped multigrain hot cereal
1/4 cup (54 grams) packed light brown sugar

ingredient_groups.title: 2-pound loaf; use INSTEAD of the 1.5-pound group
items: 1 cup (160 grams) dry finely chopped multigrain hot cereal
1/3 cup (72 grams) packed light brown sugar

instructions: Verify machine capacity and choose one loaf-size group. The publisher recommends trying the 1.5-pound batch first, even in some 2-pound machines. Neither group fits a 1-pound-only machine.
Use dry cereal made of small chopped grains and seeds, not large breakfast flakes. Do not soak it beforehand.
With the machine unplugged, remove its pan. Add milk and the remaining ingredients, with yeast last and separated from liquid and salt until mixing begins.
Install the pan, close the lid, plug in, and select the matching 1.5- or 2-pound loaf, light crust, and basic/white cycle. Start the complete cycle.
When baking finishes, unplug and remove the hot pan using oven mitts. Turn the loaf onto a rack and cool 1-2 hours before slicing.
notes: The two size groups are alternatives, never a combined batch. The publisher lists an approximately 3-hour cycle; actual duration follows the machine.
For a less sweet loaf, the source permits 1 1/2 tablespoons brown sugar in the 1.5-pound group or 2 tablespoons in the 2-pound group. It also permits an equal amount of olive oil instead of butter.
This coherent multigrain cereal formula does not reconstruct every protected manual-table variant or establish its multigrain/rapid program.

title: Finger Gelatin (Jell-O Kitchen)
attribution: Jell-O Kitchen, Kraft Heinz, Finger Gelatin
yield: One 13 by 9-inch pan, cut into small squares

items: 3 packages (3 ounces each) raspberry-flavored Jell-O gelatin
4 envelopes (1/4 ounce each) Knox unflavored gelatin

instructions: Mix both dry gelatins in a large bowl. Add the boiling water and stir until no undissolved gelatin remains.
Lightly spray a 13 by 9-inch pan and pour in the dissolved gelatin.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour and until firm, then cut into small squares.
notes: This is the manufacturer's actual complete recipe, not an invented formula from general guidance. Its full-batch envelope weights are preserved; they are not equated to the incomplete card's tablespoon measurement.
